title: CBSE CLASS 11 — Biology | Living World Biodiversity Classification
description: Subject-wise test on Living World Biodiversity Classification (Biology) for CBSE CLASS 11. 25Q.
subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The scientific naming system where each organism has a name composed of two parts, the genus and the species, is known as:

options.explanation: Polynomial nomenclature uses more than two words to name an organism, which is not the standard system.
Trinomial nomenclature uses three parts (genus, species, and subspecies), which is not the standard two-part system.
Correct. This is the standard system for naming organisms with two parts: genus and species.
Uninomial nomenclature uses a single name, which is not the standard system for species identification.

questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, proposed by Carolus Linnaeus, is a system where each organism is given a two-part name: the generic name (genus) and the specific epithet (species).
questions.hint: This system uses two Latinized words to name organisms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A collection of preserved plant specimens mounted on sheets, systematically arranged according to a universally accepted system of classification, is called a:

options.explanation: Correct. A herbarium is a collection of preserved plant specimens arranged systematically.
A botanical garden is a place where living plants are grown and displayed, not preserved specimens.
A museum may contain preserved specimens but is not specifically for plant classification.
A zoological park is for living animals, not plant specimens.

questions.explanation: A herbarium is a storehouse of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed, and preserved on sheets, along with their labels providing information about their collection.
questions.hint: This is a place where dried plant specimens are stored for study.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a defining characteristic of living organisms without any exception?

options.explanation: Growth can occur in non-living things (e.g., crystals), so it is not a defining characteristic without exception.
Some living organisms (e.g., mules) do not reproduce, so it is not a defining characteristic without exception.
Correct. All living organisms exhibit metabolism, and no non-living object does.
Consciousness is a defining characteristic but is not universal (e.g., plants may not exhibit it in the same way). Metabolism is more fundamental.

questions.explanation: While growth and reproduction are characteristics of living organisms, they are not defining characteristics without exception (e.g., non-living things can grow, some living organisms are sterile). Metabolism is a defining characteristic as all living organisms exhibit it, and no non-living object does. Consciousness is also a defining characteristic, but metabolism is a more fundamental and universal process.
questions.hint: This characteristic involves all biochemical processes in an organism.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct ascending order of taxonomic categories?

options.text: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
options.explanation: Incorrect. The order is reversed; Kingdom is the largest category, not the smallest.

options.text: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is the descending order, not ascending.

options.text: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Division/Phylum → Kingdom
options.explanation: Correct. This is the correct ascending order of taxonomic categories.

options.text: Genus → Species → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
options.explanation: Incorrect. Species comes before Genus in the hierarchy.

questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy starts with the smallest unit, Species, and progresses to Genus, Family, Order, Class, Division (for plants) / Phylum (for animals), and finally Kingdom.
questions.hint: Start from the smallest taxonomic unit and move to the largest.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the characteristics of living organisms: I. Growth is an intrinsic property in living organisms. II. Reproduction is synonymous with growth in unicellular organisms. III. Metabolism is a defining characteristic without exception. IV. Consciousness is the most obvious and technically complicated defining feature of all living organisms. Which of the above statements are correct according to NCERT?

options.explanation: Incorrect. Statement III is also correct.
Incorrect. Statements I and IV are also correct.
Incorrect. Statement III is also correct.
Correct. All statements are correct as per NCERT.

questions.explanation: I. Growth from inside is intrinsic to living organisms. II. In unicellular organisms, growth (increase in mass) and reproduction (cell division) are essentially the same. III. Metabolism is a defining feature as all living organisms exhibit it, and no non-living object does. IV. Consciousness (ability to sense environment) is indeed a defining feature, and its complexity varies, making it technically complicated.
questions.hint: All statements are correct as per NCERT Class 11 Biology textbook.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A student is tasked with identifying an unknown plant specimen collected from a new forest area. Which of the following taxonomic aids would be *most* helpful for its initial identification based on contrasting characters?

options.explanation: A monograph provides detailed information about a single taxon, not for initial identification.
A flora lists the plants of a particular area but is not primarily used for identification based on contrasting characters.
A museum contains preserved specimens but is not designed for initial identification using contrasting characters.
Correct. A taxonomic key is specifically designed for identification based on contrasting characters.

questions.explanation: A taxonomic key is used for identification of plants and animals based on similarities and dissimilarities, using a pair of contrasting characters (couplet). Monograph provides information on one taxon, Flora lists plants of an area, and Museum has preserved specimens but is not primarily for initial identification by contrasting characters.
questions.hint: This aid uses a series of paired statements to narrow down the identity of an organism.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** The 'genus' is a group of related species which has more characters in common as compared to species of other genera. **Reason (R):** Species are the lowest category in the taxonomic hierarchy and represent individual organisms.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. While A is true, R is false, so the explanation is invalid.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. R is false, so this option is invalid.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Correct. A is true, but R is false as species represent groups, not individual organisms.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect. A is true, and R is false.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true; a genus comprises a group of related species sharing more common characteristics. Reason (R) is false; while species are the lowest category, they represent groups of potentially interbreeding natural populations, not merely individual organisms.
questions.hint: Evaluate the truth of both the assertion and the reason separately.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between Taxonomy and Systematics?

options.text: Taxonomy involves identification, nomenclature, and classification, while Systematics only deals with the classification of organisms.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Systematics is broader and includes evolutionary relationships.

options.text: Taxonomy is a broader field that includes evolutionary relationships, whereas Systematics is limited to describing and naming organisms.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Taxonomy does not include evolutionary relationships; Systematics does.

options.text: Systematics is a broader field that includes taxonomy along with evolutionary relationships between organisms.
options.explanation: Correct. Systematics includes taxonomy and evolutionary relationships.

options.text: Both Taxonomy and Systematics deal exclusively with the naming and classification of newly discovered species.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Systematics also includes evolutionary relationships.

questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the process of identification, nomenclature, and classification. Systematics is a broader term that includes taxonomy and also studies the evolutionary relationships among organisms.
questions.hint: Systematics includes evolutionary relationships, while taxonomy does not.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A group of scientists discovered a new organism in a remote rainforest. They observed that it is multicellular, heterotrophic, reproduces sexually, and its cells lack a cell wall. Based on these characteristics, to which kingdom would this organism most likely be classified?

options.explanation: Incorrect. Plantae have cell walls made of cellulose and are autotrophic.
Incorrect. Fungi have cell walls made of chitin and are heterotrophic but reproduce asexually or sexually with spores.
Correct. Animalia are multicellular, heterotrophic, lack cell walls, and reproduce sexually.
Incorrect. Protista are mostly unicellular, and some have cell walls, but they are not multicellular like the organism described.

questions.explanation: The characteristics provided point to Animalia: - Multicellular and heterotrophic rule out Monera (unicellular) and most Protista. - Lack of a cell wall rules out Plantae (cellulose cell wall) and Fungi (chitin cell wall). - Sexual reproduction is common in animals. Therefore, Animalia is the most appropriate kingdom.
questions.hint: Consider the presence or absence of a cell wall and mode of nutrition.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a defining characteristic of living organisms?

options.explanation: Reproduction is a defining characteristic of living organisms.
Growth is a defining characteristic of living organisms.
Metabolism is a defining characteristic of living organisms.
Inertness (lack of activity) is not a characteristic of life.

questions.explanation: Living organisms exhibit growth (increase in mass), metabolism (sum total of life processes), and reproduction. Inertness (lack of activity) is not a characteristic of life.
questions.hint: Consider the fundamental processes that define life.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Taxonomy involves the study of:

options.explanation: Evolution is studied under evolutionary biology, not taxonomy.

options.text: Identification, naming, and classification of organisms
options.explanation: This is the core definition of taxonomy.
Ecological interactions are studied under ecology.
Genetic variation is studied under genetics.

questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the branch of biology concerned with identifying, naming, and classifying organisms based on shared characteristics.
questions.hint: Taxonomy focuses on the classification and naming of organisms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): The system of binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus. Reason (R): Binomial nomenclature uses two names to denote a species — genus and species.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true — Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature. The reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion, as binomial nomenclature uses genus and species names.
questions.hint: Evaluate the truth of both the assertion and the reason, and whether the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is placed in the kingdom Fungi?

options.explanation: Mushrooms belong to the kingdom Fungi.
Spirogyra is a green alga, classified under Protista.
Nostoc is a cyanobacterium, classified under Monera.
Amoeba is a protozoan, classified under Protista.

questions.explanation: Mushrooms are fungi. Spirogyra is a green alga, Nostoc is a cyanobacterium, and Amoeba is a protozoan — all placed in other kingdoms.
questions.hint: Consider the characteristics of fungi and other kingdoms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by:

options.explanation: Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed the three-kingdom classification system.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Carolus Linnaeus proposed the binomial nomenclature system.

questions.explanation: Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system in 1969, grouping organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
questions.hint: Recall the scientist associated with the five-kingdom classification system.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A student collected a specimen from a pond. It has chlorophyll, is unicellular, and has a rigid cell wall made of cellulose. Which kingdom does this organism most likely belong to?

options.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic and do not have chlorophyll.
Algae are unicellular, photosynthetic, and have a cellulose cell wall, classified under Protista.
Plantae are multicellular and do not fit the unicellular description.
Monera includes bacteria and cyanobacteria, which lack a cellulose cell wall.

questions.explanation: The organism is unicellular, has chlorophyll, and a cellulose cell wall — characteristics of algae, which are classified under Protista in the five-kingdom system.
questions.hint: Consider the characteristics of the specimen and match them with the kingdoms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct match of a plant group with its characteristic feature?

options.explanation: Bryophytes lack vascular tissues and seeds.
Pteridophytes are the first group to show vascular tissues.
Gymnosperms produce seeds but lack flowers.
Angiosperms produce seeds.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes (ferns and allies) are the first group to show vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). Bryophytes lack vascular tissues and seeds; gymnosperms and angiosperms produce seeds.
questions.hint: Match the plant group with its defining characteristic.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: In the three-domain system, Archaea are classified separately from Bacteria due to:

options.explanation: Both Archaea and Bacteria are prokaryotes and lack a nucleus.
Neither Archaea nor Bacteria have chloroplasts.
The three-domain system is based on differences in ribosomal RNA sequences.
Both Archaea and Bacteria are unicellular.

questions.explanation: The three-domain system (Carl Woese) separates Archaea and Bacteria based on differences in ribosomal RNA and cell membrane composition, despite both being prokaryotes.
questions.hint: Consider the molecular and structural differences between Archaea and Bacteria.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): All living organisms share a common ancestor. Reason (R): Evidence for evolution comes from fossil records, comparative anatomy, and molecular biology.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is a key principle of biology (common descent). The reason provides valid evidence supporting evolutionary theory, hence R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Evaluate the truth of both the assertion and the reason, and whether the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate hierarchical level in classification for organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring?

options.explanation: Family is a higher taxonomic rank and does not define interbreeding.
Order is a higher taxonomic rank and does not define interbreeding.
Species is defined by the ability to interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
Genus is a higher taxonomic rank and does not define interbreeding.

questions.explanation: Species is the basic unit of classification, defined as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offspring under natural conditions.
questions.hint: Consider the definition of species in the context of classification.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a defining characteristic of living organisms in the current classification system?

options.explanation: Growth is a characteristic of living organisms and is considered in classification systems.
Response to stimuli is a characteristic of living organisms but is not a defining feature in the current classification system.
Metabolism is a defining characteristic of living organisms and is considered in classification systems.
Reproduction is a defining characteristic of living organisms and is considered in classification systems.

questions.explanation: While response to stimuli is a characteristic of living organisms, it is not considered in the current classification system as a defining feature. The current system emphasizes molecular and genetic similarities for classification.
questions.hint: Think about the key features used in modern biological classification systems.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The scientific name of mango is *Mangifera indica*. Which family does it belong to?

options.explanation: Poaceae is the family of grasses, not mango.
Anacardiaceae is the correct family for mango.
Fabaceae is the family of legumes, not mango.
Rosaceae is the family of roses and related plants, not mango.

questions.explanation: *Mangifera indica* belongs to the family Anacardiaceae, commonly known as the cashew family, which includes mango and cashew.
questions.hint: Recall the family name associated with the genus *Mangifera*.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Taxonomy is the branch of biology that deals with identification, naming, and classification of organisms. Reason (R): Taxonomy helps in understanding the evolutionary relationships among organisms.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: R is true but does not correctly explain A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both statements are true, but R does not explain A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: A is true, and R is also true.

questions.explanation: Taxonomy indeed involves identification, naming, and classification of organisms (A is true). However, understanding evolutionary relationships is a broader scope that falls under systematics, not solely taxonomy (R is true but not the correct explanation of A).
questions.hint: Consider the scope of taxonomy versus systematics.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about species and classification is correct?

options.text: Only I and II are correct
options.explanation: Statement III is also correct.

options.text: I, II, and III are correct
options.explanation: All three statements are correct.

options.text: Only II and III are correct
options.explanation: Statement I is also correct.

options.text: Only I and III are correct
options.explanation: Statement II is also correct.

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Species is the basic unit of classification (I), a species can interbreed and produce fertile offspring (II), and binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus (III).
questions.hint: Recall the definitions and contributions related to species and classification.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: What is the correct hierarchical order of classification from broadest to most specific?

options.text: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
options.explanation: This is the correct hierarchical order.

options.text: Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
options.explanation: The order of Phylum and Class is incorrect.

options.text: Kingdom → Phylum → Order → Class → Family → Genus → Species
options.explanation: The order of Order and Class is incorrect.

options.text: Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Family → Order → Genus → Species
options.explanation: The order of Phylum, Class, Family, and Order is incorrect.

questions.explanation: The correct hierarchical order of classification from broadest to most specific is Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species.
questions.hint: Recall the standard taxonomic hierarchy.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A student observes two plants in the garden. Plant X has parallel venation and fibrous roots, while Plant Y has reticulate venation and tap roots. Based on these observations, which of the following is most likely correct?

options.text: Both plants belong to the same family
options.explanation: Monocots and dicots typically belong to different families.

options.text: Plant X belongs to Monocotyledons, while Plant Y belongs to Dicotyledons
options.explanation: Plant X (parallel venation, fibrous roots) is a monocot, and Plant Y (reticulate venation, tap roots) is a dicot.

options.text: Plant Y belongs to Monocotyledons, while Plant X belongs to Dicotyledons
options.explanation: Plant Y has reticulate venation and tap roots, which are dicot features.

options.text: Both plants belong to different orders but the same class
options.explanation: Monocots and dicots belong to different classes (Monocotyledonae and Dicotyledonae).

questions.explanation: Parallel venation and fibrous roots are characteristic features of Monocotyledons, while reticulate venation and tap roots are characteristic features of Dicotyledons. Therefore, Plant X is likely a monocot, and Plant Y is likely a dicot.
questions.hint: Recall the distinguishing features of monocots and dicots.
